review_scope: Versioned review of the selected SBOGZB01 status row, triggered by the pre-registered 20-project blind review (position 10, construction and location both disagreed). It decides whether the frozen lifecycle observation meets the acceptance contract in docs/expansion_200.md. The locator is reviewed separately (job-local quality44 designer-r2) and is only summarized here. The blind result is not changed: 18 of 20 agreements, gate not passed. No tracked file, frozen input, contract or release artifact was edited, and no commit or branch was created.
decision_summary: The row does not meet the contract. Its only in-window status evidence is Scala's undated portfolio card, captured 2026-07-21. Archive history shows that card was last changed when SBOGZB01 moved from In development to Under construction, between 2024-05-26 and 2024-09-25, and that its text has been identical since then. Scala's own dated FY2025 management report (signed 2026-03-26) lists the group's seven data centers under construction by location: Tamboré, Fortaleza, Lampa and Huechuraba. Bogotá is not on that list. No dated authoritative observation of SBOGZB01 work inside 2026-05-22 to 2026-08-20 was found. The 2026-07-21 retrieval cannot refresh a mid-2024 label that the operator's own later dated statement contradicts. The raw 2026-07-21 bytes are also no longer recoverable.

basis: The evidence is a categorical portfolio label whose definition ends 'among others'. It is not a dated observation of work, which is what the pre-registered definition requires.

Archive history dates the label's content: SBOGZB01 sat in a combined In-development card through 2024-05-26 and appears alone under Under construction from 2024-09-25. The card text is unchanged from then to 2026-09-17, and its start-up window is the one first given to the combined three-building card in 2022.
Scala's dated, group-wide FY2025 management report (2026-03-26) lists the seven data centers under construction at Tamboré, Fortaleza, Lampa and Huechuraba. Bogotá is not among them.
No dated in-window first-party, authority or contractor record of SBOGZB01 work was found.

By the contract's rule that a later web retrieval or page edit does not refresh an observation, and by the Frederick and Key Point precedents, the 2026-07-21 retrieval cannot turn this contradicted mid-2024 label into an in-window physical observation.

blind_disagreement_cause.construction: Mainly an Atlas evidence error. The reviewer's unable_to_verify is correct on the merits: no dated in-window physical observation exists, and the selected label is stale and contradicted by Scala's own dated report, which was public by 2026-05-03, before the Atlas capture. The CAPTCHA and the exhausted search budget limited the reviewer, but full access would have found only the same undated label (through the archive) plus contrary evidence.
blind_disagreement_cause.location: Mainly an Atlas evidence weakness. The Atlas point is the zone-wide address plate, not a project position, so even a reachable IDECA service would not have given the reviewer an SBOGZB01 point. The unreachable Catastro host and the CAPTCHA were secondary.

precedents_applied.rule: A July publication that repeats April text 'is not treated as a fresh observation'.
'The undated construction label, old start announcement and permit do not fill that gap.'
An archived company disclosure is used when the raw replay payload matches the CDX digest. Applied here to the in-window copies and the PDFs.
In the same tranche, Harch's dated construction start stays at its own date: continued availability in July 'is not a fresh physical update'.

counter_arguments_considered.argument: An undated live page is evidence as of its capture, which is within the window.
counter_arguments_considered.response: That rule dates evidence. It does not turn a categorical label into an observation of physical work. Here the label's content demonstrably dates from mid-2024, and the operator's own later dated statement contradicts it. The contract's no-refresh rule therefore governs the re-retrieval.

counter_arguments_considered.argument: Scala curates the section, and leaving SBOGZB01 visible re-affirms it.
counter_arguments_considered.response: The curation happened between 2025-01-26 and 2026-01-28, before the window. The same curation hid SGRUTB10 and SGRUTB11, which the March report appears to count as under construction, so visibility is not a reliable physical-status signal. No card changed during the window.

counter_arguments_considered.argument: The March report predates the window, so work could have started later.
counter_arguments_considered.response: Possible. But the card had said Under construction since 2024, so it cannot evidence a later start, and no other in-window record exists. The contract requires positive in-window evidence.
Its 13/7 counts are the same as Scala's report, which locates the 7 outside Colombia. Frost & Sullivan is a third party.

counter_arguments_considered.argument: A small modular SBOGZB01 might be left out of the count.
counter_arguments_considered.response: Speculative. Huechuraba (4.8 MW) is counted, and no source says modular builds are excluded.
The count is not a reason to keep an unsupported row. The contract treats partial progress as progress.
